clue.text: Reads grid, wrongly showing neglect

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are put together wrongly, that is, in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone misreads a crossword grid, which shows they are not paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges READSGRID; 'showing' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to ignore it or pay it no heed, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Dance record leading to love

indicators.note: the first piece leads, coming in front of the second

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
O is zero, love in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A song played at a dance leads to romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is a style of dancing to pop music, and a dance event with recorded music.

clue.text: Queen after time is a charmer

indicators.note: the Queen's letters come after the time in the answer

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A queen who reigns after an earlier era turns out to be charming.
explanation.walkthrough: SPELL is a period of time, as in 'a spell abroad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A speller is one who casts spells, and charm is an old word for a spell, so a charmer.

clue.text: Spot English agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Someone spots a British secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or notice, exactly as to spot.

clue.text: Relative is haggard — not good!

indicators.note: not good means the abbreviation for good is removed

parts.note: gaunt means haggard, thin and drawn

explanation.surface: A family member looks worn out, which is not a good sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' drops G (good) from GAUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family member.

clue.text: Gloomy journalist returning to be dealt with immediately

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for a journalist is read backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
a pressing matter is urgent and must be dealt with now

explanation.surface: A miserable reporter comes back to an urgent job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses ED into DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Depressing means causing low spirits, so dismal or gloomy.

clue.text: Entertains multitudes

definitions.meaning: a person who entertains guests ... them
a host is a great crowd

explanation.surface: A performer entertains vast crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to receive guests; the noun sense, as in 'a host of angels', is a large number.

clue.text: Centaur's daughter somehow ran off

indicators.note: off means not right, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A centaur's daughter galloped away by some means or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the ten letters of the two words before it; the word that looks like the anagram signal is itself fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur is half man, half horse, so a female one would be part horse, part woman; a witty twist on a rider.

clue.text: Newspaper angle for swimmer

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A newspaper looks for an angle on a story about a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a UK tabloid newspaper; 'angle' reads as a story angle but is the verb to fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sunfish is a large ocean fish, so a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Press agitated about hotel serving watered-down drinks

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, that is around, the hotel
agitated means stirred up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London

explanation.surface: Reporters get worked up about a hotel serving diluted drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' scrambles the five letters into SPERS; 'about' wraps them round the London luxury hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is wine mixed with soda water, so a diluted drink.

clue.text: Foolishly presenting pearl to investor

indicators.note: letters arranged foolishly are put in a silly new order, so this signals an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly hands a pearl to a person putting money into their venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolishly' rearranges the fifteen letters of PRESENTINGPEARL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeping partner puts capital into a business without taking part in running it, so is an investor.

clue.text: Regularly downplays exclusive

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the word is picked

explanation.surface: Someone routinely plays down a news scoop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'downplays'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusive in the sense of sole or single: the only one, excluding all others.

clue.text: Abandoned European souvenir in outskirts of Detroit

indicators.note: the European souvenir is placed in the letters taken from the city's edges
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: a relic is a keepsake or memento, a souvenir of the past

explanation.surface: A European keepsake turns up on the fringes of Detroit, a city with many abandoned buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' keeps only the city's first and last letters; 'in' sets the European souvenir between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict building or ship has been abandoned and left to decay.

clue.text: Whale upset by one caught in crazy gymnastic performances

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: the orca is the killer whale

indicators.note: one and caught go in the word for crazy

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A whale is overturned by someone caught up in a crazy stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the killer whale upside down in this down clue; 'in' puts one and caught inside the slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatics are spectacular feats of agility and balance performed by gymnasts.

clue.text: Good antique piece of tableware initially declared secure

parts.note: antique means old
a plate is an item of tableware

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A fine old plate is declared at the outset as a safe valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold-plated is used figuratively of something with assured value, as in a gold-plated guarantee or a safe investment.

clue.text: Savage female promises to accept returned Apple component

indicators.note: one piece accepting another takes it inside itself

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

indicators.note: returned means the word for the fruit's centre is read backwards

parts.note: the core is a part of an apple

explanation.surface: An angry woman's pledges involving a returned Apple computer part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes EROC; 'to accept' places it after the F and before the promises. The capital A makes 'Apple' look like the tech company.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferocious and savage are synonyms, both meaning fiercely violent or wild.

clue.text: Amazing fizzy drink gets a lot of criticism

parts.note: Fanta is a brand of fizzy orange drink

indicators.note: a lot of the word but not all, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: stick is informal for criticism, as in 'getting stick'

explanation.surface: A soft drink draws heavy criticism, which is astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims STICK to STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic means extraordinary or wonderful, so astonishingly good.

clue.text: Colour of old church, not quite red

indicators.note: not quite the whole word means its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: The stonework of an old church is a shade that is almost but not quite red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims 'red' to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment and the colour named after it.

clue.text: Is able to return home without me for food

indicators.note: to return means the word for being able is read backwards

parts.note: 'can' means is able, as in 'she can swim'

indicators.note: home without me means those two letters are removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone can go back to their house without the speaker, to get something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' makes NAC from CAN; 'without' takes ME from HOME, leaving HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip snack, so an item of food.

clue.text: Saw Charlie secured

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
locked means secured or fastened

explanation.surface: Someone saw Charlie lock up.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock something is British slang for noticing it, so clocked means saw.

clue.text: Greyish-brown grease ruined clothing

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour, used especially of horses

indicators.note: letters that are ruined are broken up and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Grease has stained and ruined some brownish clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges GREASE into GAREES.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are work trousers with a bib and braces, a type of clothing.

clue.text: Provide a detailed account of old money

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
the pound is British money

explanation.surface: Someone describes old currency in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound is the UK currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out and explain at length, so to give a full account.

clue.text: Fuss by half-hearted mob is precious

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother, as in 'much ado about nothing'

indicators.note: the word's heart is a double letter, and losing half of it leaves one

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly crowd, a mob

explanation.surface: A disorderly crowd makes a fuss over something valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two middle Bs of RABBLE, leaving RABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious in the sense of dear and lovable, as a sweet child or pet is described.

clue.text: Returned plans for tinned meat

indicators.note: returned means the word for plans is read backwards

parts.note: maps are plans or charts, and to map something out is to plan it

explanation.surface: Plans sent back about the supply of canned meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns MAPS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a brand of canned pork luncheon meat.

clue.text: Dirt around middle of step becomes softened

indicators.note: the dirt goes around the letters taken from the middle

parts.note: mud is wet dirt

indicators.note: the middle of a four-letter word is its two central letters

explanation.surface: Mud on the middle of a step has dried soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the two central letters of 'step'; 'around' wraps the dirt round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted colours or sounds are toned down, made quieter or softer.

clue.text: Adopt a pseudonym to cover exploits

indicators.note: the words cover the answer, which lies hidden inside them

explanation.surface: Someone uses a false name to conceal their adventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' finds the answer inside adopT A PSeudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap a resource is to draw on it, so to exploit it.

clue.text: Smart leaders of American college hiding expenses

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Clever heads of an American college conceal their costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' takes the first letters of 'American college hiding expenses'.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to sting or hurt, so to ache.

clue.text: Make provision for nice cat aunt took abroad

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered or spread widely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aunt takes her lovely cat overseas, which needs advance arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges NICECATAUNTTOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something into account is to allow for it in one's planning.

clue.text: Fish regularly sense ciphers

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means picking every other one of the word

explanation.surface: Fish sense patterns, as if reading secret messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of 'sense', E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a code, a system for disguising messages.

clue.text: Went down in action involving special constable before finale

indicators.note: one piece involving another encloses it

parts.note: a deed is an act or action

indicators.note: one piece comes before the other in the answer

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for a special constable, a volunteer UK police officer
the end is the finale

explanation.surface: A volunteer police officer was in action just before the climax as things went downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts the constable and finale inside the action. A special constable is a part-time volunteer police officer in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To descend is to go down, so descended is the past tense, went down.
